scope.name: W Promotional
notes: English WotC-era supplemental stamped-promo source set.
This source set deepens the seven modeled W Promotional rows and treats the gold W stamp as a legible identity rail, not as authentication.

sources.title: Local English supplemental WotC catalog: W Promotional
Bulbapedia raw wikitext: W Promotional cards (TCG)

claims.text: The local catalog models W Promotional with a September 1, 1999 release date.
The local catalog and manifest model seven W Promotional stamped-promo rows.
The local rows frame W Promotional as stamped cards drawn from existing English source sets and distributed through magazine, league, and giveaway routes.
The W Promotional identity depends on two pieces at once: the underlying source card and the stylized gold foil W stamp. The unstamped source expansion card is not enough.

W Promotional is interesting because it turns ordinary set cards into evidence of early English Pokemon distribution infrastructure: Duelist and Top Deck magazines, regional league use, and brand-partner giveaways.

The special identification instruction for this release is to preserve the W stamp, the source set identity, and the distribution note as separate legible facts before an agent treats a scan or listing as a W Promotional row.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, or agent result says W Promotional, W stamp, gold W stamp, stamped Pikachu, stamped Dark Arbok, stamped Brock's Vulpix, or Top Deck / Duelist promo.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat W Promotional as a stamped source-card identity: confirm the underlying card and the gold W stamp before using the row.
steps: Identify the underlying English source card named by the W Promotional row.
Confirm the visible stylized gold foil W stamp on the card front.
Preserve the distribution route when supplied, such as magazine issue, league route, regional giveaway, or Kraft Australia route.
Do not merge the row with the unstamped source expansion card or with a different stamped promo family.
For transactional use, ask for close photos of the W stamp, card name, set/number area, back, surface, and any packaging or provenance claimed by the seller.

narrative.human_title: The little gold W as a distribution fossil
narrative.why_it_matters: W Promotional is small, but it shows a very early English Pokemon machine learning how to reach people. A Jungle Pikachu, a Fossil Kabuto, a Team Rocket Dark Arbok, a Gym card: the card face is familiar, then a small gold W turns it into a trace of magazines, leagues, and giveaways. The stamp is the story, but only if the agent keeps it separate from the ordinary card underneath.

sources.title: Local English supplemental WotC catalog row: W Promotional Pikachu
Bulbapedia raw wikitext: W Promotional cards (TCG)

claims.text: The local W Promotional row identifies Pikachu as the stamped card derived from Jungle number 60.
The local row records The Duelist Magazine, September 1999, as the distribution note for W Promotional Pikachu.

The current supplemental W Promotional source row does not provide an illustrator credit for this stamped slice; the dossier therefore leaves the artist unset instead of importing an unstamped Jungle-row credit.
This Pikachu matters because the mascot is being routed through an early English hobby-publication channel: the familiar Jungle card becomes a magazine-contact artifact when the W stamp is present.
An agent should not accept a generic Jungle Pikachu as this row; it needs the Jungle 60 identity and the W stamp visible as separate legible features.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A user or listing says W stamp Pikachu, Duelist Pikachu, Jungle Pikachu W, or W Promotional Pikachu.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Confirm Jungle Pikachu 60 and the gold W stamp before treating the card as W Promotional Pikachu.
steps: Confirm the underlying card is English Jungle Pikachu number 60.
Confirm a visible stylized gold W stamp on the card front.
Keep The Duelist Magazine September 1999 route as a distribution note, not as proof of physical provenance.
Do not merge with unstamped Jungle Pikachu or other early Pikachu promos.
For a trade, ask for close photos of the W stamp, the card number/set area, the full front, the back, and surface/edge condition.

narrative.human_title: A magazine mark on the mascot
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest W Promotional story: everyone recognizes Jungle Pikachu, but the little gold W changes the job of the card. It stops being only a set card and starts being a record of how early English Pokemon reached hobby readers. The whole trick is not to let the mascot swallow the stamp.

narrative.human_title: A reprint memory with another mark
narrative.why_it_matters: Wartortle is a neat little stack of history. For an agent, the row only makes sense if both layers stay visible.
